scope: Final evaluation results are independent of search selection. Implementation descriptions use the inspectable retained source, without claiming byte-identical final-snapshot identity.

claims.claim: The final evaluation completed and qualified; qualification is not proof of broad generalization.
The retained original reference has zero measured search score change; three alternative evaluations are unscored and do not establish measured losses or failure causes.
The pooled studied score is 0.9527636891 and equivalent normalized MAE is 0.0472363109; rounded values in the abstract, results, and pooled table are 0.9528 and 0.0472.
Random-query low-rank pooled score is 0.9364101694, equivalent MAE 0.0635898306; the studied-minus-random difference is 0.0163535197.
The supplied pooled paired family-clustered interval against random-query factors is [0.0148071678, 0.0184780194], not an interval against ridge or for subgroups.
Information-selected ridge scores 0.9482262260 (MAE 0.0517737740), with descriptive studied-minus-ridge difference 0.0045374631 and no supplied paired significance interval.
Medoid ridge scores 0.9327472830 (MAE 0.0672527170), mean offset 0.9206056682 (MAE 0.0793943318), and historical means 0.9068768878 (MAE 0.0931231122).
The studied method has the highest pooled observed score among the six evaluated policies, without statistical superiority being established against all comparators.
Three final seeds are 1009, 1013, 1019; replay is excluded from primary means and figures.
Figure 2, supplementary Table 2, and derived_results.json retain each of the twelve primary source/split/seed cells and six policies, using control=false and replay=false.
The studied policy has higher observed scores than random-query factors in all twelve retained primary cells and the highest three-seed mean in each of four source/split conditions.
Studied condition means are 0.9496/0.9442 for MTEB model/family splits and 0.9591/0.9582 for Open LLM model/family splits, rounded from saved observations.
Pooled source scores are 0.9468974985 for MTEB and 0.9586298797 for Open LLM; they do not constitute controlled source-difficulty comparisons.
Open LLM family split at seed 1019 gives studied score 0.9531041725 versus information-selected ridge 0.9533160600, a retained local reversal.
Pooled independently deranged-history score is 0.9233917542 and actual-minus-control gap is 0.0293719349.

Every retained source/split/seed pair has a lower observed studied-policy score under historical-column derangement, as shown in Figure 3 and supplementary Table 3; the contrast changes learning, querying, and target composition jointly.
The final required cases completed and reset replay passed; these are interface/execution controls, not comprehensive validity guarantees.

Supplementary Figure 4 shows only the studied-policy measured checkpoint arrays, increasing in each retained actual trajectory; no baseline checkpoint comparison, fixed-panel curve, or universally sufficient budget is inferred.
Recorded seed durations are 24.0816306723, 22.8890082091, 23.0760153015 seconds, excluding independent acquisition; no measured inference-cost, end-to-end storage, or speed advantage is asserted.

The inspectable retained source implements masked alternating ridge factors, fixed observed column means, and SVD initialization; lambda=0.1, candidate ranks 1/2/4/8, seeded 10% cell validation, at most four validation sweeps and eight refit sweeps capped by requested steps.
Equations 1 and 3 describe clipped remaining-target 1-MAE and context-independent ridge latent prediction; availability is known and historical missing cells are masked, not observed zeros.

The retained-source acquisition in Equation 4 uses a unit-noise quadratic trace-reduction proxy, includes the queried coordinate, and ignores purchased score values. Equation 5 is a fixed-target matrix identity, not an MAE optimality theorem.

Random LF uses matching reference factor fit/prediction construction; the ridge comparators use zero-filled centered covariance and penalties 0.01/0.1/1 chosen with every-fifth-row historical validation; means and mean-offset policies use random legal queries.

The readable retained and original reference files match, but exact byte-level identity to the separately hashed final snapshot is not independently certified; mechanism interpretation is conditional on supplied-source association.
The evaluated source regimes are separately fitted MTEB embedding-model scores and Open LLM six raw generative benchmark columns; no learned cross-source transfer is asserted.

Pinned MTEB revision is 6dabbcc68c28ea5f180ce7df79347b3ca9cc6383; pinned Open LLM revision is 9c09a7cae43334062a82cb164f2ef255013dafa2. MTEB extraction uses natural-bound original test scores and default/English task/revision/subset columns; Open LLM uses raw scores. The latter dataset license is undeclared.

The inspected final protocol uses model and heuristic name-family disjoint groups, approximately 70% historical groups, twenty-observation MTEB column support, and coverage filters; family labels are not authoritative lineage.
MTEB checkpoints are 1/2/4/8, Open LLM checkpoints 1/2/3. Target, row, checkpoint, seed, split, source weighting is nested and equal at each level; control/replay have zero primary weight.

The supplied interval uses 200 paired family-clustered bootstrap draws with RNG24681357 and 2.5/97.5 percentile endpoints, shared family multiplicities across paired policies, cases and seeds within source. It is preserved, not reconstructed from seed means.

Documented evaluation versions are CPython3.12.15, NumPy1.26.4, SciPy1.12.0, PyArrow16.1.0, with CPU operation, isolation and broker requirements; this is not a newly measured cross-platform reproduction.

No fixed untouched target panel, response-adaptive selector, controlled nonlinear superiority, universal budget sufficiency, or family-held-out tuning is supported. Diagnostic descriptions remain unverified.

MMLU, MTEB and HELM motivate heterogeneous evaluation coverage; item-level compression in tinyBenchmarks and metabench differs from buying aggregated benchmark scores; BenchBench motivates care about agreement methodology.
Observational scaling laws and Sloth motivate low-dimensional multi-benchmark capability descriptions, without establishing interpreted skill recovery or scaling-law estimation by this study.

Matrix factorization, probabilistic/Bayesian factor models, and implicit-feedback models provide distinct methodological precedents; this study fits regularized numerical-score coordinates rather than a fully Bayesian or implicit-preference model.
Convex, spectral, and alternating matrix completion methods have assumption-dependent guarantees that are not verified for the selectively observed matrices here.
Ridge regularization, Bayesian design and statistical active learning are methodological context for the inspected solves and proxy, not evidence of novel architecture or universal MAE optimality.

Missing-data assumptions and incomplete-data likelihood methods are separate from merely optimizing a masked loss; generic bootstrap and dependent-array resampling motivate specifying the resampling unit.
